title: THE CURTAIN AND THE WAY IN

memory_verse.label: Bible Reference
memory_verse.text: "They made the curtain of blue, purple and scarlet yarn and finely twisted linen, with cherubim woven into it by a skilled worker. They made four posts of acacia wood for it and overlaid them with gold. They made gold hooks for them and cast their four silver bases." - Exod 36:35-36 (NIV)

devotion.label: Devotion
devotion.text:
This is the inner curtain — the one that separated the Most Holy Place from everything else. Behind it sat the ark. Before it, no one could pass except the high priest, once a year, with blood (Heb 9:7).

Cherubim were woven into it, just as cherubim guarded Eden's gate (Gen 3:24). The message was unmistakable: God is holy, and sinners cannot simply walk in.

For fifteen centuries that curtain hung, and every generation understood what it meant. Access to God was restricted.

Then, on a Friday afternoon outside Jerusalem, Jesus cried out and gave up His spirit — and the temple curtain was torn in two from top to bottom (Matt 27:51). Top to bottom. Torn from God's side, not ours. No human hand did that.

Hebrews spells out what it means: we now have confidence to enter the Most Holy Place by the blood of Jesus, by a new and living way opened for us through the curtain, that is, His body (Heb 10:19-20).

The curtain that kept people out has become the doorway that brings us in.

If you have ever felt that God is distant, or that you are not welcome in His presence, look at the torn curtain. That was God's answer.

reflection.label: Reflection
reflection.text:
1. Do you approach God with confidence or with fear of being unwelcome?
2. What does it mean that the curtain was torn from the top?
3. Are you living in the access Christ purchased for you?

prayer.label: Prayer
prayer.text: Lord Jesus, You opened the way through Your own body. Thank You that I may come in with confidence. Amen.
